Note::TexAccessor::int_norm¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::TexAccessor::int_norm() const

Collapse Multi-Integral Commands To \int¶

int_norm() rewrites the double/triple/quadruple and contour integral commands — \iint, \iiint, \iiiint, \oint, \oiint, and \oiiint — to the plain \int. Use it to normalize integral notation before counting, diffing, or otherwise comparing math source that mixes these spellings; a plain \int is already left as-is.

The match requires a word boundary immediately after the command name. A subscript written with _ does not create that boundary, because _ counts as a word character in the underlying regex engine: \oint_C and \iint_D are not rewritten, while \oint\, or \oint (a following space or any other non-word character) are. This is the sharpest edge case of the method — contour and multi-integrals with an attached region subscript, a very common real notation, pass through unchanged.

The operation is shape-preserving, cell-independent, and returns a fresh Note. Undefined input remains undefined; Bool, Int64, Float64, and Bytes receivers are rejected because TeX source is Text.

Example 1: Every Recognized Spelling¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note(
    {"\\iint f \\, dA, \\oint_C, \\iiiint, \\oiint, \\oiiint"})
    .tex().int_norm()
    << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\\int f \\, dA, \\oint_C, \\int, \\int, \\int"]

\iint, \iiiint, \oiint, and \oiiint all become \int. \oint_C does not, because the _C subscript attaches directly with no word boundary between t and _ — see the note above.

Example 2: A Plain \int Is Already Canonical¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"\\int_0^1 x\\,dx"}).tex().int_norm()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["\\int_0^1 x\\,dx"]

Example 3: A Shape-Preserving Batch¶

std::cout << pluss::make_note({"\\iint_D f\\,dA", "\\int already"})
              .tex().int_norm()
          << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["\\iint_D f\\,dA", "\\int already"]

Both cells are unchanged: the first because _D blocks the boundary match exactly as in Example 1, the second because it is already \int.

Example 4: Undefined And Non-Text Input¶

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().tex().int_norm().defined()
          << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2}).tex().int_norm();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false
Int64: rejected

See Also¶

  • limit_norm: strip \limits/\nolimits, which commonly follow an integral or summation command.

  • sum_norm: the equivalent collapse for \sum spelling variants.
